onmanorama.title: FSSAI flags Bisleri water as unsafe, company says bromate within prescribed limit | India News | Onmanorama
onmanorama.h1: FSSAI flags Bisleri water as unsafe, company says bromate within prescribed limit
onmanorama.text: Join WhatsApp Channel EXPERIENCE NOW MONDAY, NOV 23, 2026 TODAY'S E-PAPER KERALA NEWS ENTERTAINMENT SPORTS INDIA WORLD BUSINESS COLUMNS VIDEOS TRAVEL FOOD HEALTH UPSC ADVERTISEMENT NEWS INDIA FSSAI flags Bisleri water as unsafe, company says bromate within prescribed limit Onmanorama Staff PUBLISHED: NOVEMBER 23, 2026 04:38 PM IST 2 MINUTE READ IN BRIEF Comments Bisleri packaged drinking water bottles are stacked inside a shop for sale in Kolkata, India, March 12, 2026. File photo: REUTERS/Sahiba Chawdhary ADVERTISEMENT FOLLOW US New Delhi: A day after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International over an allegedly unsafe packaged drinking water sample, the company on Monday maintained that its product was safe for consumption and said it would cooperate with the regulator. In a statement, Bisleri said it had not received any notice from the FSSAI and claimed that a referral laboratory had found the bromate level in the sample to be within the prescribed limit. The company said the case dates back around 14 months and concerns a batch manufactured in September 2025 at its Goa facility, one of 143 plants in its network. According to Bisleri, the FSSAI collected six samples from the facility on September 30, 2025. Initial tests found that five samples met all applicable standards. The sixth, however, recorded a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the permissible limit of 10 micrograms per litre. Following an appeal by the company on November 22, 2025, the FSSAI sent the sample to a referral laboratory for further testing. "The referral laboratory found bromate of the sample within the prescribed limit and separately flagged polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the sample," Bisleri said. The company said the differing test results prompted it to get the sample independently tested at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, which also found the bromate level to be within the permissible limit. Bisleri submitted the independent test results to the FSSAI's Western Regional Office along with a formal letter dated February 2, 2026. It said it had received no further communication from the regulator and had assumed the matter was closed. ADVERTISEMENT The company also claimed that it had not received any notice either by email or in hard copy and was unable to locate the reported notice on the FSSAI website. "Drinking water safety is a priority for Bisleri. We maintain stringent quality controls of over 90 tests across our 10-step manufacturing process," the statement said. Bisleri said it would continue to cooperate with the FSSAI and address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process. southmatters.title: Bisleri Prosecution: FSSAI Flags Unsafe Water Sample
southmatters.h1: FSSAI Orders Prosecution of Bisleri After Water Sample Fails Safety Tests
southmatters.text: Sign in Home Andhra Pradesh Karnataka Keralam Tamil Nadu Telangana Entertainment Editorial World News National Sports SIGN IN Welcome!Log into your account your username your password Forgot your password? PASSWORD RECOVERY Recover your password your email Home Andhra Pradesh Karnataka Keralam Tamil Nadu More FSSAI Orders Prosecution of Bisleri After Water Sample Fails Safety Tests HOMENATIONAL By DK Reddy November 23, 2026 6:18 PM IST India’s food regulator has sanctioned the Bisleri prosecution after a sample of the company’s packaged drinking water was declared unsafe. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) announced the action against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd on its official social media handles on Sunday, November 22. Discover more Read Daily News News Learn Hindi The sample failed two rounds of testing. The case will now be taken to court under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. What Happened According to FSSAI, food safety officials collected a regulatory sample of “Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)” from Bisleri International’s premises. The regulator did not name the city, the plant or the batch. In the first test, the sample did not meet the prescribed limits for bromate. It was declared unsafe under the FSS Act. The company then appealed, and the sample was sent to a Referral Food Laboratory for a second analysis. The referral laboratory also declared the sample unsafe, but for a different reason. It detected polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). FSSAI said several PAHs can be toxic when they cross safe levels. The regulator said the findings established violations relating to unsafe food, and it granted sanction to prosecute. Company: Bisleri International Pvt Ltd Product: Packaged drinking water (not mineral water) First lab: Bromate above prescribed limits Referral lab: PAHs detected Action: Prosecution sanctioned under the FSS Act, 2006 Why the Bisleri Prosecution Matters Bisleri is one of the most widely sold bottled water brands in India, so the action has drawn wide attention. FSSAI already treats packaged drinking water as a high-risk food category, which means stricter inspections and audits for makers. Discover more SOUTH South India Buy Maps It is important to note what the action does and does not mean. A prosecution sanction allows the case to go before a court. It is not a conviction. FSSAI has not announced a recall of Bisleri water, and it has not said the finding applies to products beyond the tested sample. Bisleri has not issued a public statement on the action so far. Business Standard reported that the company did not reply to its request for comment. Other Companies in the Same Crackdown Bisleri was one of several food businesses named in the same FSSAI update. The regulator also sanctioned prosecution against Vasant Masala and Tit-Bit Foods over chilli powder samples with pesticide residues above limits. A Tit-Bit Foods turmeric sample was found to contain excess tin. Mimansa Industries faces prosecution over a walnut kernel sample, while Asha Confectionery was ordered to recall chocolate-filled cookies found unsafe. The licences of Urmi Lifesciences and Gaur Ayurvedic Store were suspended over serious violations. What’s Next The case will now move to the courts, where Bisleri can contest the findings. FSSAI has stepped up enforcement this year against food businesses, e-commerce firms and beverage makers. Consumers with concerns about a food product can raise complaints through FSSAI’s official grievance channels. e4m.h1: Bisleri says packaged water is safe, questions FSSAI test findings in Goa sample case
e4m.text: Home Marketing News Bisleri says packaged water is safe, questions FSSAI test findings in Goa sample case Bisleri says packaged water is safe, questions FSSAI test findings in Goa sample case The company says independent testing found bromate levels within prescribed limits and maintains it has not received any formal notice from the food safety regulator by e4m Desk Published: Nov 23, 2026 11:17 AM | 2 MIN READ Follow Us Show Quick Read AI-assisted summary, reviewed by our newsroom ▼ Bisleri International has maintained that its packaged drinking water is safe for consumption, responding to reports of regulatory action by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over a sample that reportedly failed safety tests. The company has questioned the findings, citing subsequent independent testing that found bromate levels within prescribed limits. In a statement, Bisleri said the matter relates to a batch manufactured in September 2025 at its Goa facility. On September 30, 2025, FSSAI collected six samples from the plant, of which five were found to meet all applicable standards. The sixth sample recorded a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre. Following an appeal by Bisleri on November 22, 2025, the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for retesting. While the referral laboratory found the bromate level to be within the prescribed limit, it separately flagged the presence of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Bisleri said the difference between the test results prompted it to get the same sample tested independently at an FSSAI-approved laboratory. The independent test also found bromate levels within the prescribed limit, according to the company. The company said it submitted these test results to FSSAI's Western Regional Office through a formal communication dated February 2, 2026. It added that it received no further communication from the regulator following the submission and had understood the matter to be closed. Bisleri also said it had not received any notice from FSSAI, either by email or in hard copy, and had been unable to locate the reported notice on the regulator's website. Reiterating its focus on product quality, the company said it conducts more than 90 tests across its 10-step manufacturing process. It added that it would continue to cooperate with FSSAI and address any concerns through the appropriate regulatory process. "A trusted brand for years, Bisleri remains safe for consumption," the company said in its statement.
